title: Redstrike Cross-Model Exhaustion Review
description: The verdict artifact (runtime/exhaustion_review.json) written by the model-pinned, cross-model exhaustion-adversary agent. After the mechanical + semantic + recall gates pass, this independent reviewer's sole job is to DISPROVE the 'engagement complete / class exhausted' claim: it reads the ledgers, findings, the recall-audit output and the audit trail and hunts for the gaps the deterministic gates can't see (categories marked attempted/done with no depth substance, hosts/surface with no evidence artifacts, blocked marks never re-driven, signalled surfaces with shallow clears, feeder findings never chained). A no_gaps_found verdict is required (and every gap it ever raised must be closed) before the engagement is report-ready. Because the reviewer runs on a DIFFERENT, pinned model than the executor and its same-model *-verify reviewer, a shared-model 'we're done' blind spot can't pass it. The verdict is the whole point of the pin: this is NOT a same-model self-check.

verdict.description: no_gaps_found = the adversary could not disprove exhaustion (every raised gap is closed or genuinely-unclosable with a named blocker) → report-ready; found_gaps = at least one open gap remains → NOT report-ready, re-drive it.

model.description: the PINNED model the adversary ran on — MUST differ from the executor / primary *-verify reviewer model. The cross-model pin is the whole point; a same-model 'are we done?' check is worthless.

checked.description: the inputs the adversary actually read (e.g. coverage_ledger, surface_ledger, findings, recall_audit, audit_trail) — so a vacuous review is visible.

gaps.description: every exhaustion gap the adversary raised. For a no_gaps_found verdict this is normally empty; a genuinely-unclosable gap may remain here ONLY with status=closed/resolved/redriven AND a named blocker (an honest 'couldn't, because X', never a silent drop).

diversity.description: OPTIONAL — the MEASURED cross-model diversity state (roadmap L-H), recorded by the adversary/orchestrator from runtime/model_ledger.json so the deliverable states whether the `model:` pin actually yielded a different dispatched model. The free-text `model` field above stays (self-reported); this block is the measured cross-check. Absent on older reviews (backward-compatible). When cross_model is false, name the blocker — a documented limitation, surfaced, never a silent same-model pass.

cross_model.description: true iff the exhaustion-adversary (or a `*-verify` reviewer) actually ran on a DIFFERENT model family than the executors, per the model ledger.

executor_models.description: the distinct model families the executors actually ran on (from the model ledger).

adversary_model.description: the model family the exhaustion-adversary actually ran on (from the model ledger), which may DIFFER from the self-reported `model` field above when a safeguard forced a fallback.

blocker.description: when cross_model is false, the named reason the alternate model was unavailable (e.g. safeguard-terminated-subagents / single-model-available) — an honest 'same-model, because X', not a silent pass.

gap.description: one concrete exhaustion gap: WHERE it is (a category and/or a host/surface), WHAT was missed, and the concrete remediation that would close it.

category.description: the vulnerability class / coverage category the gap belongs to (e.g. sqli).

host.description: the host / surface element the gap belongs to when it is not class-scoped (e.g. api.acme.com).

type.description: the gap kind — e.g. no-depth-substance, no-evidence-artifact, blocked-never-redriven, shallow-clear, feeder-finding-unchained.

gap.description: the concrete miss the adversary found (one honest sentence).

remediation.description: the concrete action that would close it (escalate X / test host Y / chain finding Z / re-drive the blocked class).

severity.description: how material the gap is to the 'complete' claim.

blocker.description: when a gap is genuinely unclosable in-scope, the named environmental reason (e.g. no-oob-collaborator, single-identity) — an honest 'couldn't, because X'.

status.description: open = still outstanding (forces found_gaps); redriven/resolved/closed = accounted for. A no_gaps_found verdict may carry only non-open gaps.
